THIS MFA FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLE ACT PRAYING TO ENHANCE AND AWARD RS.89,20,000/- (RUPEES EIGHTY-NINE LAKH TWENTY THOUSAND ONLY) AS JUST COMPENSATION AS AGAISNT RS.6,78,920/- (RUPEES SIX LAKH SEVENTY-EIGHT THOUSAND NINE HUNDRED TWENTY ONLY) AWARDED IN MVC NO.5249/2018 BY JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26.11.2019,
PASSED BY THE I-ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE AND MACT, BENGALURU.
 THIS MFA, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
DR.CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA .J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT Heard Sri Jagadish S.Halashetti, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri H.C.Vrushabhendraiah, learned counsel who is representing respondent No.2 - insurance company.
NC: 2024:KHC:21261-DB 2.
With a version that the amount awarded as compensation is inadequate, the claimant is before this Court.

Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru in MVC No.5249/2018 dated 26.11.2019.
3.
The appellant in the capacity of injured filed an application claiming compensation of Rs.89,20,000/-.
The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.6,78,920/-.

4. Making his submission with regard to the merits of the matter, learned counsel Sri Jagadish S.Halashetti submits that the appellant sustained grievous injuries due to the accident and became permanently disabled.

Though through the evidence of PW.2, the nature of injuries sustained, the treatment taken and the aspect of disability were established and likewise though through the evidence of PW.3 and Ex.P13, the income of the appellant was established, the Tribunal erred and Raghu H T vs Praveen Singh on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106359192/
2 arrived at a wrong conclusion and awarded a meager sum as compensation NC:

sentences.text: and therefore, the compensation granted requires enhancement.

5. On the other hand, Sri H.C.Vrushabhendraiah learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the Tribunal has awarded excess amount as compensation and indeed the appellant is not entitled to such a huge sum.
Learned counsel further submits that as respondent No.2 failed to contest the matter, he could not raise sufficient grounds attacking the evidence produced by the appellant.

Learned counsel ultimately seeks to dismiss the appeal by confirming the order of the Tribunal.
6.

A perusal of the record goes to show that the Tribunal has awarded compensation under the following heads:
 SL.No. Heads Amount  1 Pain and agony Rs.20,000-00
2 Medical Expenses Rs.64,120-00  NC: 2024:KHC:21261-DB
3 Food, attendant, Rs.19,800-00  conveyance, nourishment  and other incidental charges  etc.
4 Loss
of income
during laid Rs.25,000-00  up period
5 Loss of earning capacity Rs.4,80,000-00  6 Loss of amenities in life Rs.20,000-00  7
Future medical expenses Rs.50,000-00  TOTAL Rs.6,78,920-00 7.
It is not in dispute that the appellant sustained comminuted fracture of the medial tibial condyle involving the joint.
Also it is not in dispute that an operation i.e., open reduction and internal fixation of the proximal tibial medial condyle with T plate and screws under spinal anesthesia was done.
Further, it is brought on record that the appellant was again operated for removal of implant.
Likewise by all the evidence produced, the appellant has established that he took treatment as in-patient from 06.06.2017 to 10.08.2017.

3 NC: 2024:KHC:21261-DB 8. Taking disability in respect of whole body as 10% and earning as Rs.25,000/- p.m., the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.4,80,000/- under the head loss of earning.

sentences.text: This Court is of the view there are no grounds to interfere with such a finding.
However, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- only towards loss of income during laid up period.
Through the evidence of PW.3 and Ex.P13 the appellant has established that he was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
The appellant took treatment as in- patient for more than two months.
Therefore, granting compensation under the head loss of earnings for a period of one month is unjustifiable.
Therefore, this Court considers desirable to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rs.25,000 x 3) towards loss of income during laid up period.

9. Likewise having considered the nature of injuries sustained and the treatment taken, this Court is of the view the amount awarded as compensation under the head pain and agony i.e., Rs.20,000/- is required to be NC: 2024:KHC:21261-DB enhanced.
The just amount that can be awarded under this head is Rs.50,000/-.

Also having considered the occupation of the appellant as Driver by the date of accident and the nature of injury sustained, this Court is of the view under head loss of amenities in life, an additional sum of Rs.20,000/- is required to be awarded.
Therefore, the total enhancement in compensation would be Rs.1,00,000/-.

Thus, in the light of foregoing discussion, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.

ii) The amount awarded as compensation by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru through orders in MVC No.5249/2018 dated 26.11.2019 is enhanced by Rs.1,00,000/-.
iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
NC: 2024:KHC:21261-DB iv) The second respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
v) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.
Registry is directed to transmit the entire record to the concerned Tribunal immediately.
